record.title: FRESH reports higher tool-task completion with failure-aware graph memory
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint proposes FRESH, which stores successful actions, failures, preconditions and repairs in a typed experience graph, then retrieves compact guidance for a frozen language-model executor. On tau-bench, its authors report the highest average pass performance among compared memory methods for three backbones, with average relative gains over no-memory baselines of 10.8% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 38.9% for Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and 53.2% for Qwen3-8B. On AppWorld, it reports pass rates of 0.268 vs 0.250 on Test-N and 0.146 vs 0.115 on Test-C versus the strongest listed baseline. The absolute AppWorld rates remain low; all results are author-reported benchmark outcomes and were not independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On tau-bench, the authors report FRESH has the highest average pass performance among compared memory methods for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B, with average relative gains over each no-memory baseline of 10.8%, 38.9% and 53.2%, respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On AppWorld, the authors report task pass rates of 0.268 on Test-N and 0.146 on Test-C for FRESH, versus 0.250 and 0.115 for the strongest listed baseline. FRESH also reports 9.4 vs 9.9 average steps on Test-N and 10.0 vs 10.4 on Test-C.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported tau-bench/AppWorld results and failure-aware graph pipeline have not been independently run or audited.
Benchmark gains do not establish transfer to live APIs, changing policies, or high-consequence state-changing actions.

brief.importance_rationale: If the failure-aware memory gains transfer, they could meaningfully improve tool-task completion and action reliability for small and medium language-model agents. A 4 reflects a useful systems result; the evidence is author-reported on two benchmark suites, with low absolute AppWorld pass rates and no independent reproduction.
limitations: All results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The AppWorld pass rates remain low in absolute terms: 0.268 on Test-N and 0.146 on Test-C, compared with strongest listed baseline rates of 0.250 and 0.115.
The reported gains apply to tau-bench and AppWorld benchmark splits with the specified historical trajectories and execution budgets; real-world tool environments are not established.
The paper describes ablations, but the inspected tables do not provide uncertainty intervals for the headline gains.
The action gate's safety and policy compliance were not independently audited; reported task completion is not proof of safe deployment.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint proposes FRESH, which stores successful actions, failures, preconditions and repairs in a typed experience graph, then retrieves compact guidance for a frozen language-model executor. On tau-bench, its authors report the highest average pass performance among compared memory methods for three backbones, with average relative gains over no-memory baselines of 10.8% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 38.9% for Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and 53.2% for Qwen3-8B. technical.claimed_result: The authors report that FRESH improves task pass results over no-memory and existing memory baselines on tau-bench and AppWorld across three frozen open-source model backbones, using a graph retriever and action precondition gate.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint describes the method and reports benchmark tables and ablations. The outcomes remain author-reported; no code, data or benchmark run was independently verified in this activation.
technical.implementation_status: The paper describes an implemented evaluation with graph construction, learned retrieval and policy/precondition gating. A public runnable repository was not inspected in this review.
technical.mechanism: FRESH converts successful and failed tool trajectories into a typed graph of tasks, actions, observations, errors, preconditions and repairs. A graph retriever provides compact Do/Avoid/Check/Repair guidance to a frozen executor; state-changing and policy-sensitive actions pass a live precondition gate.
technical.regime: tau-bench Airline and Retail plus AppWorld normal and challenging splits; three frozen open-source backbones: Gemma-4-26B-A4B, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B. The graph and retriever are frozen on held-out test tasks.
technical.reproducibility: The paper gives benchmark setup, baselines, model names and tables; this activation did not inspect a runnable artifact or reproduce the results. No uncertainty intervals were found in the inspected result sections.
technical.strongest_baseline: The no-memory agent is the reference for reported relative gains; AppWorld Test-N/Test-C comparisons use the strongest listed baseline task pass rates of 0.250 and 0.115, respectively.

brief.title: FRESH reports higher tool-task completion with failure-aware graph memory
brief.why_it_matters: Tool-using agents can repeat failed calls, miss action preconditions or perform unsafe state changes. FRESH combines structured memory of both successes and failures with a gate for state-changing actions, and reports gains across several small and medium backbones on two tool-use benchmarks. The reported pass rates and relative gains are confined to those benchmark splits; they do not establish reliable real-world operation or the safety of the gate.
